G-F101.trick: Arachnoid granulations = one-way drains that let CSF seep back into the venous sinus blood.
G-F101.tip: CSF path ends at the arachnoid granulations → dural venous sinus. Blocked drainage can cause hydrocephalus.

G-F102.trick: Ventral horn = motor "Vroom" neurons that send commands out. Dorsal horn = sensory input.
G-F102.tip: Gray horns hold cell bodies. White columns hold long tracts. Ventral = motor, dorsal = sensory.

G-F103.trick: CAUDA EQUINA = horse's tail: loose nerve roots below where the cord ends (around L1–L2).
G-F103.tip: A lumbar puncture goes below L2 because only floating nerve roots (cauda equina) are there, not the cord.

G-F104.trick: Interneuron = the middleman connecting incoming sensory and outgoing motor neurons.
G-F104.tip: Interneurons live entirely in the CNS and integrate signals. Monosynaptic reflexes skip them.

G-F105.trick: OCCIPITAL = the Optic lobe at the back of your head ("eyes in the back of your head").
G-F105.tip: Lobes: frontal (planning, motor), parietal (touch), temporal (hearing), occipital (vision).

G-F106.trick: MEDULLA = the Main line that connects brain to spinal cord and runs breathing and heart rate.
G-F106.tip: Brainstem order, top to bottom: midbrain → pons → medulla oblongata → spinal cord.

G-F107.trick: THALAMUS = the Train station: most sensory trains stop here before going to the cortex.
G-F107.tip: Thalamus relays sensation (except smell). Hypothalamus runs homeostasis (temperature, hunger, hormones).

G-F108.trick: LR6 SO4, the rest are 3: Lateral Rectus = CN VI (abducens ABducts the eye).
G-F108.tip: Can't look outward to one side? Think abducens nerve (VI).

G-F109.trick: PARAsympathetic = CRANIOsacral, ganglia right next to the organ (long first neuron, short second).
G-F109.tip: Sympathetic = thoracolumbar, ganglia near the spinal cord. Parasympathetic = craniosacral, ganglia near the target.

G-F110.trick: At every autonomic ganglion, ACh hits Nicotinic receptors: "Ganglia go Nic."
G-F110.tip: Both divisions use ACh on nicotinic receptors at the ganglion. They differ at the target organ.

C-ch11-protection.trick: CSF = the brain's water cushion and shock absorber.
C-ch11-protection.tip: CSF is made by choroid plexuses in the ventricles and flows in the subarachnoid space.

C-ch11-cord.trick: CONUS = cone-shaped tip where the cord ends (about L1–L2).
C-ch11-cord.tip: Below the conus medullaris lie the cauda equina and the filum terminale.

C-ch11-reflex.trick: Reflex arc in 5 steps: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Integration center → Motor neuron → Effector ("Real Smart Interns Make Errors").
C-ch11-reflex.tip: Reflexes are fast and automatic. Know all five parts and their order.

C-ch11-cerebrum.trick: CORTEX = the bark (cortex) on the outside of the brain: thin gray matter.
C-ch11-cerebrum.tip: Gray matter = cell bodies (cortex, nuclei). White matter = myelinated tracts underneath.

C-ch11-brainstem.tip: Thalamus = relay. Hypothalamus = homeostasis. Cerebellum = coordination and balance.

C-ch11-cranial.trick: PLEXUS = a braided rope: nerves weave and regroup (cervical, brachial, lumbar, sacral).
C-ch11-cranial.tip: A plexus mixes fibers from several spinal nerves, so one root injury rarely paralyzes a whole limb.

C-ch11-autonomic.trick: ANS = Automatic Nervous System: heart, smooth muscle, glands, without you thinking.
C-ch11-autonomic.tip: Autonomic = involuntary targets with a two-neuron chain. Somatic = skeletal muscle with one neuron.

C-ch11-disorders.trick: HYDRO-CEPHALUS = water (hydro) on the brain (cephalus): CSF builds up and ventricles swell.
C-ch11-disorders.tip: In infants, hydrocephalus shows as a growing head and bulging fontanels because skull sutures aren't fused.
